role_declaration: Design engineer. The practice starts with one question: what does the system receiving this actually need? Not what I need from it. What it needs from me. That question has governed twenty-five years of work across print shops, enterprise platforms, brand systems, and AI.

manifesto.short:
Twelve students in a self-contained classroom in Brooklyn. Every subject, every accommodation. A kid hears "solve for the missing number, show your work, and explain your reasoning" and starts working on the first instruction. The rest is gone. Not because the student can't do the work. Because the task was designed for a processing profile that isn't theirs.

That classroom taught me to ask one question before designing anything: what does the system receiving this actually need? Twenty-five years later the question still governs the work. Enterprise platforms, brand systems, AI governance. The material changes. The person on the other end doesn't.
manifesto.content:
Twelve students in a self-contained classroom in Brooklyn. Every subject, every accommodation. A kid hears "solve for the missing number, show your work, and explain your reasoning" and starts working on the first instruction. The rest is gone. Not because the student can't do the work. Because the task was designed for a processing profile that isn't theirs.

That classroom taught me to ask one question before designing anything: what does the system receiving this actually need? Twenty-five years later the question still governs the work. Enterprise platforms, brand systems, AI governance. The material changes. The person on the other end doesn't.

My wife had a real jewelry brand and no way to show it through a screen. I built the brand system, the photography pipeline, and the platform together. One system, not three departments. She runs the business. A platform I started building in 2013 is still running, serving organizations you'd recognize. I still work alongside the person who wrote the original software.

The same question built all of it. This site was compiled from three years of my own thinking by the system described on it.

routes.name: WRITING
routes.definition: The framework. The arguments. The proof.
routes.description: Accommodation design started in a classroom in Sunset Park. The whitepaper documents the framework. The essays unpack it piece by piece. Everything here is the thinking that produced the tools and the systems.

artifacts.title: ACCOMMODATION DESIGN
artifacts.context: The AI governance field asks how to constrain the model. This paper asks what the model actually needs to do the job. The question comes from a special education classroom in Brooklyn.
artifacts.spec: A whitepaper applying special education pedagogy to AI system architecture. Task decomposition as cognitive accommodation. Evaluation systems as differentiated assessment. Prompt architecture as IEP design.
artifacts.result: Published framework with DOI. Six applied tools. The production site was compiled using the system described in the paper.

artifacts.title: ESSAYS
artifacts.context: Fourteen essays on design practice, accommodation, AI governance, and why they're the same discipline.
artifacts.spec: Each essay unpacks one piece of the practice: the classroom origin, processing profiles, input inversion, lens extraction, voice governance. Standalone introductions before the full series.
artifacts.result: Published and growing. The mini-series on accommodation design frames the whitepaper for practitioners in any field.

routes.name: SYSTEMS
routes.description: Twelve years on an enterprise platform. A jewelry brand built from scratch. Design and print production tools built to own the workflow end to end. Every one of these has to keep working after I leave the room.

artifacts.title: ENCORE
artifacts.context: A solid Windows Forms application serving some of the largest organizations in the world. The software was good. The delivery layer was about to become the constraint.
artifacts.spec: Made the case for moving to the browser, then built the whole front end from scratch.
artifacts.result: Twelve years in, the industry went browser-based. The call held. I'm still there.

artifacts.title: AIDEN JAE
artifacts.context: A trained artist designing fine jewelry from recycled solid gold. She had the product and the expertise. No brand, no platform, no way to put it in front of a stranger.
artifacts.spec: Built the entire system from scratch: brand identity, photography (camera and post), custom Shopify architecture, packaging concepts. One integrated system, not three departments.
artifacts.result: A running business. The quality comes through the screen because every piece of the system was designed to show it.

artifacts.title: SOVEREIGN DESIGN ENGINE
artifacts.context: Three projects needed physical artifacts simultaneously. The production tool was InDesign on a different machine. Every context switch broke the flow.
artifacts.spec: Images and data go in, print-ready pages come out. The software handles page geometry, data extraction, and layout. Every measurement resolves to a fixed value in inches or points. No manual layout.
artifacts.result: Three template types producing print-ready output through the same engine. Photogeography tabloids, Versagrams posters, Deep Cuts book spreads. The context switch eliminated.

artifacts.title: PRESSWORKS
artifacts.context: I came up in print shops in Brooklyn and Fort Lauderdale. Color separation, plate registration, halftone screening. The process has a logic that digital tools never captured.
artifacts.spec: A programmatic press that runs from the terminal. Separate into color plates. Screen each plate at a controllable halftone frequency. Offset registration per channel. Recombine with ink color and blend mode. ImageMagick underneath, bash on top.
artifacts.result: Sixteen operations, three bundled presets. Every parameter exposed. Every texture on this site came through PressWorks.

routes.name: TOOLS
routes.definition: The methodology. Built from the practice, used to build everything else.
routes.description: Savepoint Syntax started the morning I lost six weeks of thinking. Formwork came from watching contributors contradict decisions that lived in my head instead of in the project. The Aetherwright came from watching creative work lose its founding logic to drift. Every one of these begins with a failure that kept recurring.

artifacts.title: FORMWORK
artifacts.context: One perspective produces imitation. Multiple perspectives without structure produces noise. Evaluation happens as a single pass with no way to locate where structural concerns and identity concerns disagree.
artifacts.spec: A layered evaluation and construction system. Distinct layers of concern, each staffed with lenses extracted from real practitioners, run independently and read together. The maker resolves the disagreements. Transfers to any medium.
artifacts.result: Every project page on this site was produced by this system. The framework runs across design, culinary, and any field where craft has practitioners whose judgment you trust.

artifacts.title: SAVEPOINT SYNTAX
artifacts.context: You're in the middle of a session and your thinking changes direction. Every tool saves what you said. None of them mark where it turned.
artifacts.spec: A tag you drop in the middle of your thinking to mark the moment something clicked. One line. Writable by hand. Machine-readable. Doesn't stop the flow.
artifacts.result: Open source. Three versions. The first reproduced the exact loss it was built to prevent. Works across solo work, team conversations, and AI sessions. When you come back weeks later, you find your way in.

artifacts.title: ORDER OF THE AETHERWRIGHT
artifacts.context: I'd been getting consistent results for thirty years but I couldn't explain the method. It was instinct. You can't teach instinct, and it erodes when things get busy.
artifacts.spec: A classification system for creative work: glyphs that mark every domain, a living rulebook, a daily practice. Formalize the method the way you'd formalize a brand. Give it structure and people actually follow it.
artifacts.result: The glyph system classifies every project on this site. Now I can point to the method, explain it, and it doesn't disappear when I'm not paying attention.
